chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no believer, nor any infidel, except that he comes to his family at the decline of the sun. So when he sees his family doing righteous deeds, he praises Allah for that; and when the infidel sees his family doing righteous deeds, regret befalls him.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reaction between a believer and an infidel when seeing their family perform righteous deeds?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the psychological and spiritual impact of witnessing familial piety, emphasizing that righteous deeds serve as a source of gratitude (*shukr*) for the believer and a poignant regret (*hasrah*) for the disbeliever. Scholarly context suggests this reflects the Shia understanding of the soul's continued connection to the worldly sphere, where the moral state of one's household serves as a mirror for the individual's own spiritual standing. The contrast underscores the internal peace derived from faith versus the lingering sorrow of those who recognize truth but do not act upon it.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a Believer, nor an Infidel except that he comes over to his family at the (start of the) decline of the sun. So when he sees his family doing righteous deeds, he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon that; and when the Infidel sees his family doing righteous deeds, there would be regret upon him’ (for his lost opportunity).
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

every believing and unbeliever person visits his family everyday just after midday. If he finds his family performing good deeds, he praises and thanks Allah for this. When an unbeliever finds his family in good deeds, he laments and regrets (for his lost opportunities).”
